adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — Public members endpoint accepts an unbounded client-supplied limit (e.g. limit=10000000 on a large automatic group), letting anyone force huge queries/serialization.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new pagination code sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and uses it directly in `group.users...limit(limit)` and serialization without any maximum cap. This allows a client to pass an arbitrarily large `limit` (e.g., 10,000,000), potentially forcing very large queries and responses (DoS risk).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:23 — Negative limit/offset are passed straight to SQL, so PostgreSQL raises "OFFSET/LIMIT must not be negative" and the request fails with a 500 instead of being clamped.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then directly applies `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no clamping/validation to prevent negative values, so a request with `limit=-1` or `offset=-10` will generate SQL with a negative LIMIT/OFFSET, which PostgreSQL rejects (raising an error and resulting in a 500). This behavior is now applied for all groups (not just automatic ones), so the issue is at least exposed more broadly by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:89 — remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id) on a has_many :through, which deletes the join row without GroupUser destroy callbacks, so title/primary_group/user_count side effects can be skipped.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#remove_member, the diff changes member removal logic to `group.users.delete(user_id)` rather than using the group’s higher-level API (`group.remove(user)`), which is still used elsewhere (e.g., `add_members` uses `group.add(user)`). Using the association’s `delete` on a has_many :through typically bypasses model-level removal logic and callbacks that `group.remove` might implement (e.g., maintaining counters/side effects), so this change can introduce skipped side effects compared to the prior behavior that called `group.remove(user)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — add_members splits on "," without stripping, so " bob" silently fails to match a user, and unknown usernames are dropped while the endpoint still returns success.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and passes each raw token to `User.find_by_username(username)` without trimming whitespace (e.g. `" bob"` won’t match). It also silently skips unknown usernames (`if user = ...`) and still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, even if zero users were added. This behavior is directly shown in the diff and can lead to surprising/broken “add members” behavior for common comma+space input.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:73 — group.add on a persisted group inserts each row immediately inside the loop with no transaction, so an existing member or a failure partway through leaves a partial add (or a 500) before group.save runs.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the diff shows `usernames.split(",").each` calling `group.add(user)` inside the loop, and only afterward calling `group.save`. There is no explicit transaction or error handling around the multi-add operation, so atomicity/partial-success behavior is not guaranteed by this code. However, whether `group.add` immediately persists rows, raises on duplicates, or can produce a 500 cannot be verified from this diff alone (it depends on `Group#add` implementation), so the finding is a valid review concern but not a provable defect from the PR diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:13 — totalPages uses floor(user_count/limit)+1, so an exact multiple (e.g. 50 members, limit 50) reports an extra page, and "next" moves to an empty page.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:43 — After removeMember, findMembers reuses the stale offset, so removing the last member on the last page shows an empty page instead of stepping back.

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group.removeMember`, the success handler calls `self.findMembers()` without adjusting `offset`. `findMembers` computes the request offset using the *current* `user_count` (`Math.min(this.get("user_count"), this.get("offset"))`), but after a deletion `user_count` is still the pre-delete value until the fetch returns. If you delete the last user on the last page (e.g., `limit=50`, `offset=50`, `user_count` drops from 51 to 50), the reload request is sent with `offset=50`, and the server (now with only 50 users) returns an empty `members` array, leaving the UI on an empty page instead of stepping back a page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:6 — The public group members page now only shows the first 50 members and has no pagination controls, so the rest can't be reached.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always return a paginated slice (`limit` defaults to 50, `offset` param) rather than the full member list. On the public route (`discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`), `setupController` now just calls `model.findMembers()` once, and the public template (`discourse/templates/group/members.hbs`) has no pagination UI or actions to change `offset`/request further pages. Pagination controls were added only to the admin group page template. From the diff alone, the public members page will only ever show the first page (50) with no way to reach the rest.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:61 — addMembers never clears the usernames input and neither add nor remove handles ajax rejection, so failures are silent and re-clicking Add re-submits the same usernames.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `actions.addMembers` in `admin-group.js.es6` which explicitly notes `// TODO: should clear the input` and does not reset `this.get("usernames")` after submitting, so the input value will persist and a second click will re-submit the same usernames. Also, both `addMembers` (`this.get("model").addMembers(...)`) and `removeMember` (`self.get("model").removeMember(member)`) trigger AJAX via `Group.addMembers/removeMember` but do not attach any rejection handling in the controller/template flow, so failures would not surface unless handled elsewhere. This is a concrete UX/robustness gap introduced by the change, but not a strictly verifiable correctness break from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:13 — If the server ever returns limit=0 (e.g. limit=0 is passed through), currentPage/totalPages divide by zero and render NaN/Infinity.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `currentPage` and `totalPages` compute `Math.floor(offset / limit) + 1` and `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` but only guard on `user_count == 0`, not `limit`. In `GroupsController#members`, `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i`, so a request with `limit=0` will produce `meta.limit = 0`, which `Group.findMembers` copies into the model/controller (`self.setProperties({ limit: result.meta.limit, ... })`). That makes the division by zero path real, yielding `Infinity/NaN` in the UI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:117 — The remove_member automatic-group spec uses xhr :put instead of :delete and a magic group_id 1, so it passes on the action name no matter which route verb is used.

spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:93 — The add_members 422 spec uses magic group_id 1 and a nonexistent username and never checks that membership is unchanged, so a 422 for any reason makes it pass.

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` under `context ".add_members"`, the test `"cannot add members to automatic groups"` calls `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1, usernames: "l77t"` and only asserts `response.status.should == 422`. This relies on a magic `group_id: 1` being an automatic group (no setup in this spec block) and does not verify that no membership change occurred (e.g., user count unchanged). As written, it only checks the status code, so it’s a brittle/weak test for the new automatic-group guard in `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:50 — The update spec depends on fixture group id 1 being automatic, and nothing covers the new members pagination endpoint (limit/offset/meta).

adjudication.rationale: The spec is brittle: in `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` the new update example hard-codes `id: 1` (`xhr :put, :update, id: 1...`) and then calls `Group.find(1)` while asserting automatic-group behavior, without fabricating or setting up an automatic group in the test. That makes the test depend on an implicit fixture/seed state not shown in the diff. Also, the diff changes `GroupsController#members` to a paginated JSON shape with `meta: { total, limit, offset }` and `members:` (in `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb`), but no new spec is added to assert this new pagination contract, even though the JS `Discourse.Group#findMembers` now depends on `result.meta.*` and `result.members`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/routes/admin_group_route.js:13 — Members load fire-and-forget in setupController, so the member section renders empty or stale and a failed request is swallowed; a newly created group also shows the members section with no fetch done.

app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:28 — Public GET /groups/:name/members response changed from a bare array to {members, meta} with no versioning, breaking any external API/plugin consumer that iterates the array.

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a bare JSON array) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }` (object with `members` and `meta`) in `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb`. Internal Ember code is updated to consume `result.members`/`result.meta` (`Discourse.Group#findMembers`), but there is no versioning or compatibility shim shown in the diff, so any external client/plugin expecting an array from `GET /groups/:name/members(.json)` could break. This is a concrete compatibility concern, though not necessarily an internal functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:38 — PATCH /admin/groups/:id with changes[add]/changes[delete] is no longer handled but still routes to update, which returns 200 without changing membership and silently sets visible=false since params[:visible] is absent.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, Admin::GroupsController removed the PATCH-specific membership handler (`update_patch`) and the `request.patch?` branch, leaving a single `update` method that always does `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` and never processes `params[:changes]` (see `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb` update). Rails resource routing still provides PATCH /admin/groups/:id to `update` (no change in `config/routes.rb` to remove it). Therefore a PATCH request that previously sent only `changes[add]/changes[delete]` will now (a) not change membership and (b) set `visible` to false when `params[:visible]` is absent (since `nil == "true"` => false) while still returning success if the save succeeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:24 — Create/update stop reading the nested group[...] params, so existing API callers that send group[name] get a blank-name error on create and have visibility silently reset to false and alias_level/name ignored on update.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Admin::GroupsController#create and #update to read top-level params (e.g., `params[:name]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:alias_level]`) instead of the previously accepted nested `params[:group][...]` payload. In `create`, `group.name = (params[:name] || '').strip` will become blank if a caller still sends `group[name]`, and `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` will default to false if omitted. In `update`, `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` will silently reset visibility to false when `visible` is not provided, and `alias_level`/`name` will be ignored if still sent under `group[...]`. This is a concrete behavior change/regression visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22 — usernames on POST/PUT /admin/groups is now dropped silently (200 with no membership change) rather than rejected, so callers that set members during create/update lose data without any error.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, Admin::GroupsController#create now only reads `params[:name]` and `params[:visible]` and never applies any `usernames` parameter (previously `params[:group][:usernames]` was used). Likewise, `update` no longer reads `usernames` at all (previously `payload[:usernames]`). Both actions still return success (create renders the group on save; update renders `success_json`) without validating/rejecting unexpected membership params, so a client sending usernames during create/update will get 200 but no membership changes, i.e., silent data loss/regression. Membership changes were moved to new `add_members`/`remove_member` endpoints, but the old behavior isn’t rejected or flagged.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — /groups/:name/members now defaults to limit 50 for all groups (before, non-automatic groups returned all members and automatic groups returned 200), so non-paginating consumers quietly get truncated lists.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff changes the query to always apply `limit`/`offset` with a new default `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. Previously, only `automatic?` groups were paginated (default 200), while non-automatic groups returned all members (no limit/offset). This is a behavior/API change that will truncate results to 50 for callers that don't pass pagination params, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — New add_members only accepts usernames as a comma-separated string; an array param (usernames[]=), which was accepted by the old changes[add] Array() handling, raises NoMethodError and returns 500.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` is immediately used as `usernames.split(",")`. If the request supplies `usernames[]=` parameters (parsed by Rails as an Array), `Array#split` does not exist and will raise `NoMethodError`, causing a 500. The prior implementation used `Array(actions[:add]).each`, which tolerated both strings and arrays; this diff removes that tolerance without type-checking/coercion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:19 — totalPages uses floor(user_count/limit)+1, so exact multiples of limit (e.g. 50 members) report an extra empty page and "next" navigates to an empty page (should be ceil).
matched_golden_ids: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same pagination bug: using Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 adds an extra page when user_count is exactly divisible by limit, leading to navigation to an empty page, and suggests using ceil instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:59 — next clamps offset to user_count (not last page start), so combined with the totalPages off-by-one it can request offset == total and render an empty member list.
matched_golden_ids: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that clamping the next offset to user_count can yield offset == total, which results in an empty member list on the last page. This is the same underlying UX/logic issue described in the golden comment (empty page when total equals limit/last page).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:47 — After removing the only member on the last page, findMembers reuses the now-past-the-end offset and shows an empty page instead of stepping back.

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group#removeMember`, it calls `self.findMembers()` without adjusting `offset`. In `findMembers`, the request offset is clamped using the *current* `this.get("user_count")` (`Math.min(this.get("user_count"), ...)`), which is stale immediately after a deletion. If you delete the only member on the last page (e.g., `user_count` drops from 51 to 50 while `offset` remains 50), `findMembers` will still request `offset=50`, and `GroupsController#members` will return an empty `members` array because it applies `limit(...).offset(offset)` with the now-smaller total. Nothing in the diff steps the offset back to the previous page, so the UI can get stuck on an empty page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:684 — limit/offset are unvalidated: limit=0 makes the client divide by zero (NaN/Infinity pages), negative values cause a SQL error (500), and huge limits bypass pagination.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff introduces `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and uses them directly in `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no bounds checks. This enables `limit=0`, which then propagates to the client: `admin-group.js.es6` computes `currentPage`/`totalPages` via `Math.floor(offset / limit)` and `Math.floor(user_count / limit)`, causing `Infinity/NaN` when `limit` is 0. Negative `offset`/`limit` are also not prevented and can trigger DB/AR errors (e.g., negative OFFSET). There is also no cap on `limit`, so very large values can bypass intended pagination.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:6 — Public group members page now shows only the first 50 members and has no pagination controls, a regression from listing all members of non-automatic groups.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply `limit = (params[:limit] || 50)` and `offset`, removing the prior behavior where only automatic groups were paginated and non-automatic groups returned the full list. On the client side, the public template `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` is updated only to iterate `{{#each m in members}}`, but no pagination controls are added anywhere in that template or route, so the public members page will only show the first page (default 50) with no UI to navigate further.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:620 — add_members calls group.add for users who are already members, which likely hits the group_users unique constraint and returns 500 instead of skipping them.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `add_members` action (Admin::GroupsController), the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and calls `group.add(user)` for each found user without checking whether the user is already a member. The diff does not show `Group#add`’s behavior, so it’s not verifiable from this PR alone that this will hit a unique constraint and 500, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded edge-case risk introduced/exposed by the new endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:647 — group.users.delete(user_id) raises RecordNotFound (404) for non-members and deletes the has_many-through join row without GroupUser destroy callbacks.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the diff adds `group.users.delete(user_id)` (new code). Using `delete` on an association removes the join row without instantiating/destroying the join model, so any `destroy` callbacks on the has-many-through join (e.g., `GroupUser`) would be skipped. The finding’s claim that this *definitely* raises `RecordNotFound` for non-members isn’t directly verifiable from the diff (depends on Rails association behavior and whether the id is in-scope), but the callback-bypass concern is real and diff-grounded and could be behaviorally important.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:950 — remove_member automatic-group spec uses xhr :put, but the route is DELETE, so it doesn't exercise the real verb.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:44 — removeMember/addMembers have no rejection handling, so 422 errors (e.g. automatic group) fail silently in the admin UI.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`, `removeMember` and `addMembers` call `Discourse.ajax(...).then(function() { self.findMembers(); })` without any rejection handling, and the admin controller actions (`removeMember`, `addMembers` in `admin-group.js.es6`) also don’t attach `.catch`/error UI. The diff shows these endpoints can return 422 for automatic groups (`Admin::GroupsController#add_members`/`#remove_member`), but the diff does not prove whether `Discourse.ajax` has a global error handler that would surface the 422 to the user, so “fail silently” isn’t fully verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:21 — findMembers now returns undefined instead of a promise when name is empty, which breaks the promise contract for callers that chain .then (e.g. next/previous actions return it).
matched_golden_ids: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe a missing/implicit return causing some execution paths to yield undefined. The candidate pinpoints a specific branch (empty name) where findMembers returns undefined instead of the expected promise, which is the same underlying issue as the golden comment about code paths without explicit returns returning undefined.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:40 — Shared public Discourse.Group model now hardcodes admin-only endpoints (/admin/groups/:id/members) in removeMember/addMembers, leaking admin concerns into the non-admin model layer.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `removeMember` and `addMembers` methods to the shared `Discourse.Group` model (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js) that call admin-only endpoints (`/admin/groups/:id/members.json` via DELETE/PUT). This mixes admin concerns into the generic group model used elsewhere (e.g., non-admin group members route now calls `model.findMembers()` on the same model), which is an architecture/scope issue introduced by the change, even if those methods are currently only invoked from the admin controller/template.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:10 — Pagination state (limit/offset/members) is stored on the domain model instance and mutated by both admin controller and findMembers, mixing view paging state into the shared model.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds paging fields directly to `Discourse.Group` (`limit`, `offset`, `user_count` at the top of `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`) and `findMembers()` mutates the same model instance via `self.setProperties({ user_count, limit, offset, members: ... })`. The admin controller’s `next`/`previous` actions then also mutate `group.offset` (`group.set("offset", offset)` in `admin-group.js.es6`) and call `group.findMembers()`. This confirms pagination/UI state (offset/limit/current member page) is being stored and mutated on the shared domain model rather than being isolated to a controller/route state, which is an architectural/scope concern introduced by this change but not a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:51 — addMembers and removeMember duplicate the same ajax-to-members-endpoint-then-reload logic, differing only in verb and payload.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js: both removeMember and addMembers call the same /admin/groups/:id/members.json endpoint via Discourse.ajax and then, in a .then, reload by calling self.findMembers(). They differ only in HTTP verb (DELETE vs PUT) and payload (user_id vs usernames), so this is concrete duplicated logic/maintainability concern rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:21 — findMembers now returns undefined (`return ;`) instead of a promise on the empty-name path, giving the method an inconsistent return type.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`, `findMembers` now short-circuits with `if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return ; }`, which returns `undefined` instead of a promise. Previously it returned `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`. Since the normal path returns `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` (a promise), this change makes the return type inconsistent and can break any caller that expects `findMembers()` to be thenable (as it was before).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:82 — Stray syntax: `{ return };` misplaced semicolon, and missing semicolon after `})` at line 59.

adjudication.rationale: In `group.js` the code `if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return ; }` is valid JavaScript (it returns `undefined`), not “stray syntax” or a syntax error. Likewise, the missing semicolon after the `}).then(function() { ... })` chain in `addMembers` is not a verifiable defect from the diff—JavaScript does not require semicolons and this does not inherently break execution. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:62 — TODO ("should clear the input") left in shipped addMembers action; input is never cleared after adding.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the new `addMembers` action includes a `// TODO: should clear the input` comment and only calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` without ever resetting `this.set("usernames", ...)`. Since the template binds `{{user-selector usernames=usernames ...}}`, the entered usernames will remain in the input after adding. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:29 — next/previous actions duplicate the same get-model/clamp-offset/set/findMembers sequence; paging math belongs in one helper on the model.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the newly added `next` and `previous` actions both repeat the same pattern: `var group = this.get("model")`, compute a clamped `offset` (`Math.min(...)` vs `Math.max(...)`), `group.set("offset", offset)`, then `return group.findMembers();`. This is real duplication introduced by the diff and suggests the paging/offset clamping could be centralized (e.g., a model helper like `group.pageNext()` / `group.setOffsetClamped()`), but it does not constitute a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:13 — totalPages uses floor(user_count/limit)+1, which overcounts by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 members shows 1/2) so showingLast never matches correctly.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` (with only a `user_count==0` guard). When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 50/50), this returns 2 instead of 1, creating an extra empty page. This also interacts with `next` setting `offset` up to `user_count`, so `offset=50` yields `currentPage=2` but the server will return no members for `offset==total`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group_member.hbs:1 — Item-view template references `automatic` and targets `removeMember`, relying on implicit context leakage from the parent controller into the group-member itemView rather than passing them explicitly.

adjudication.rationale: In `group.hbs` the list is rendered with `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`, and the new `group-member` itemView (`app/assets/javascripts/admin/views/group-member.js.es6`) does not define/bind any `automatic` property or a `member` alias. Yet `admin/templates/group_member.hbs` references `automatic` and uses `{{action "removeMember" member}}`, implying it expects parent/controller context (and a `member` binding) to be available inside the itemView template. From what the diff shows, neither `automatic` nor `member` is explicitly passed/bound into the itemView, so these lookups are likely undefined in the item template and can break the conditional/remove link behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/routes/admin_group_route.js:13 — findMembers is fired without returning its promise from setupController (same pattern duplicated in discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:11), so load errors are swallowed and the route no longer waits on data.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that findMembers is invoked asynchronously without properly handling/returning its promise in setupController, meaning the route/controller may proceed before member data is available (race condition) and errors may be ignored.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:92 — add_members/remove_member duplicate find-group/automatic-guard/save-or-error boilerplate, and group.save after group.users.delete is a no-op save that obscures intent.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members and #remove_member, the diff shows repeated boilerplate: both methods do `group = Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i)`, guard `return can_not_modify_automatic if group.automatic`, then conditionally `render json: success_json` vs `render_json_error(group)` based on `group.save`. In `remove_member`, the key operation is `group.users.delete(user_id)`, which typically persists the join-table change immediately; the subsequent `group.save` does not clearly relate to the deletion and can obscure intent (even if it returns true). This is a maintainability/clarity concern rather than a verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:101 — Indentation style of methods under `protected` (and `private` in groups_controller.rb:40) changed to indented form in an unrelated reformat, inconsistent with surrounding files and adding diff noise.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — Page-size default 50 is duplicated as a magic number on server and client (group.js:10) with no shared constant or upper bound on the limit param.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:115 — remove_member "automatic" spec uses :put while the route is DELETE, and specs at lines 52/94/115 rely on magic id 1 being a seeded automatic group instead of fabricating one.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/admin/admin_base.scss:463 — Groups styles are split between the shared `.groups, .badges` block (line 164) and a second `.groups` block that leans on multiple `!important` overrides.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — Public members endpoint accepts an uncapped client-supplied limit, so ?limit=1000000 materializes and serializes every member of large (e.g. automatic trust_level) groups in one request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — add_members does one User.find_by_username query plus one insert per username over an unbounded comma list (N+1) instead of a single User.where(username_lower: ...) batch lookup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:25 — Every members page request runs a separate full COUNT(*) over the group's users join, which is costly for large automatic groups and is repeated on each pagination click.

This is a performance/scalability concern grounded in the new code, not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — Public members endpoint accepts an unbounded client-supplied limit, allowing a single request to dump every member of any visible group (including large automatic groups previously capped at 200) and causing heavy queries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:23 — Negative limit/offset values are passed straight to SQL LIMIT/OFFSET, triggering a PostgreSQL error and a 500 response instead of validated input.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are used directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no validation/clamping. adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:98 — Removed coverage for silently ignoring nonexistent usernames when adding members; add_members has no nonexistent/duplicate-username test

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes prior spec coverage that explicitly asserted adding a non-existent username succeeds silently (previously under the PATCH incremental update tests). The new membership API is `add_members` (Admin::GroupsController#add_members), which still silently ignores unknown usernames via `if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end`, but the updated specs only cover adding valid users and the automatic-group restriction; there is no test for nonexistent or duplicate usernames for `add_members`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:119 — Removed coverage for removing a non-member; remove_member (`group.users.delete(user_id)`) has no test for non-member or unknown user_id

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces the old incremental PATCH membership update tests (which included “succeeds silently when removing non-members” and adding non-existent users) with new endpoints `add_members`/`remove_member`. The new `remove_member` implementation in `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb` does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then saves, but `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` only tests removing an existing member and rejecting automatic groups—there is no test for deleting a non-member or an unknown `user_id`, so prior edge-case coverage was removed for this new logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:34 — Create spec no longer asserts a successful create with members/visible flag, only name stripping

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:20 — Group model findMembers/addMembers/removeMember rewritten to consume meta and new admin endpoints with no JS test changes

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows significant rewrites in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`: `findMembers` now calls `/groups/:name/members.json` and expects `{members, meta}` to set `user_count/limit/offset/members`, and new `addMembers`/`removeMember` call new admin endpoints (`/admin/groups/:id/members.json` PUT/DELETE) and trigger reloads. adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:91 — add_members/remove_member missing-parameter (params.require) paths are untested

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController, the new member-management endpoints use `params.require` (e.g., `group = Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i)`, `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` in `add_members`; and `user_id = params.require(:user_id).to_i` in `remove_member`). The added specs exercise success/automatic-group cases but always supply these parameters; they do not cover the `ActionController::ParameterMissing` paths when `group_id`, `usernames`, or `user_id` are omitted. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing test for new parameter-validation logic, not an immediate functional defect.
